solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Try going round the bend in reverse

indicators.note: something going in reverse travels backwards, so the word for mad is read from its end

parts.note: bats is slang for mad, crazy

explanation.surface: A learner driver is told to attempt a corner while backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to make an attempt, so stab is a noun synonym of try.

clue.text: Nick, wings clipped, leaves…

indicators.note: clipping a bird's wings trims its outer edges, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: A clipped bird is said to fly off, the ellipsis carrying the story into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue for the surface only; tea leaves are the dried leaves brewed in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea in its dry form is the shredded leaves of the tea plant, as in tea leaves.

clue.text: … a Labour politician with courage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Ed ..., a former Labour cabinet minister
second meaning: slang for nerve or guts

explanation.walkthrough: Read on from the previous clue, the surface has a nicker leaving with a brave MP. Ed Balls was a British Labour Party minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname names a real Labour politician, and the same word is vulgar British slang for bravery or nerve.

clue.text: Perhaps the Oxford team did boast after quarrelling

indicators.note: after places the boasting word behind the quarrelling word in the final order

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: The Oxford side brag once their squabble is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Crew as a past tense of crow (crowed) is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries. The Boat Race between Oxford and Cambridge is a famous annual rowing contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford University eight in the Boat Race is an example of a rowing crew, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Check on the papers

parts.note: the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: An editor runs a quick look over the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an urge or a reaction is to hold it back, which is to repress it.

clue.text: Knowledgeable English composer beginning to emerge ruddy fat

parts.note: well up in a subject means well informed about it
Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

explanation.surface: A learned English composer starts to appear with a red, plump face.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-upholstered is a jokey idiom for plump, likening padding on a body to the stuffing in a sofa.

clue.text: One head supports another making a vegetarian dish

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece supporting another sits beside it in the column, so the two are simply joined

parts.note: loaf is also slang for head, as in use your loaf

explanation.surface: One head of a team backs another while preparing a meatless meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are slang for head; 'supports' only places one next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut loaf is a baked savoury loaf of chopped nuts, a classic meat-free main course.

clue.text: Gay vicar embraces female spy Mata, creating uproar

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within one's arms, so one piece sits inside the other
gay in its older sense of merry or frolicsome suggests letters skipping about

parts.note: Mata Hari was the famous female spy of the First World War; her other name is wanted

explanation.surface: A cheerful clergyman hugs a famous spy and causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is used in its old sense of merry. The spy goes inside after the first letter of the jumbled word, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade of pots and pans, hence any din or uproar.

clue.text: Awfully short heiress longs to be a stunner

indicators.note: done awfully means botched, so the letters end up badly arranged
something cut short loses its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: A rather small rich heiress yearns to be thought beautiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of the heiress's height, but it trims the word's final letter before the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: An English rose is an idiom for a fair-skinned, classically beautiful English woman, a stunner.

clue.text: Beer and punch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for beer

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drinks order, beer and a bowl of punch; both are senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallop is old British slang for ale or beer, and as a noun it also means a hard hit.

clue.text: Being sluggish, back pair of Plymouth Argyle get beaten

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
the back pair of a word are its final two letters

explanation.surface: A football report: Plymouth Argyle, playing slowly, are defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: Plymouth Argyle is an English football club; the club name splits so that only the end of Plymouth joins Argyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is the state of being sluggish; the gerund phrase works as a noun naming that condition.

clue.text: French philosopher has no truck at first for union stuff

indicators.note: having no something means going without it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride gathers for her marriage

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: A French thinker has no dealings with trade union matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' looks like a trade union, but it is a marriage; 'at first' picks the initial of truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the eighteenth-century Genevan-French philosopher of The Social Contract.

clue.text: No good Doc can forego change in agreement

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged
no good means without G, the abbreviation for good, so that letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, losing its G

explanation.surface: A doctor declares that a change is no good and can be skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' looks like the start of the sentence, but it tells you to drop G from forego.
explanation.definitionFit: Of one accord is an idiom meaning unanimous, everyone sharing the same view.

clue.text: Root and Cook batting after introduction of off-spinner

indicators.note: after puts the cook-and-batting pieces behind the opening letter
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to cook the books is to rig them, falsify
a batsman who is batting is in

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: England's Joe Root and Alastair Cook bat after a spinner comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: Root and Cook are famous England batsmen, so 'Root' hides as a name; it is the definition. An off-spinner is a type of slow bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of something is its source or starting point, its origin.

clue.text: Kitchen apprentice sounding extremely left wing

indicators.note: sounding tells us to go by how the words are said rather than how they are written

parts.note: the chief commie is the most extreme left-winger; commie is slang for communist

explanation.surface: A trainee cook is said to hold very radical politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Commis is pronounced like commie, and chef is French for chief; the sound match is approximate.
explanation.definitionFit: A commis chef is the junior trainee cook in a professional kitchen brigade.

clue.text: Sharia foremost for haji in Mecca? Out of order for a Hindu

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper sequence, so the letters get rearranged
the foremost part of each word is its first letter

parts.note: first letters of haji, in and Mecca

explanation.surface: Islamic law, Mecca pilgrims and a Hindu figure mixed together: a scolding that something is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Islamic surface vocabulary misleads; the answer is a Hindu title. A haji is someone who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu sage or spiritual teacher, so the word names a Hindu person.

clue.text: One cast like Cinders

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: An actor chosen to play Cinderella in the pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinders is the pantomime nickname for Cinderella, so the surface is about casting a panto; the definition means cinders as ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means covered in or resembling ash, which is what cinders are.

clue.text: It's OK over in outskirts of Hackney

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the kept letters are read backwards
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the letters at both ends are kept

parts.note: the first two and last two letters of Hackney

explanation.surface: Someone reassures a friend that things are fine over on the edge of Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the outskirts are two letters at each end, not just one. Hackney is a borough of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is casual speech for yes, a reply agreeing that something is all right.

clue.text: Exaggeration shown in misshapen oil painting, not the highest class

definitions.note: noun defining a verb phrase; the gerund piling it on is the act of exaggerating

indicators.note: misshapen means deformed, so the letters lose their original arrangement
not tells us the following item is to be left out

parts.note: A is the top grade or class

explanation.surface: An art critic sees overstatement in a botched, second-rate oil painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Piling it on is an idiom for overstating things, so exaggeration describes it.

clue.text: For each jerk I lost a stone!

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so the named letter disappears from the word

explanation.surface: A dieter boasts that each jolt helped them shed a stone in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A stone' looks like fourteen pounds of weight loss but is a gem. One I goes from IDIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a variety of olivine, so it is a precious stone.

clue.text: Place for cuttings developed in Surrey newsroom primarily

indicators.note: developed means grown or changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
primarily points to the first letter only

explanation.surface: A local newspaper office in Surrey is where press cuttings were filed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuttings' suggests newspaper clippings in a newsroom; it means plant cuttings. Surrey is a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant nursery is where cuttings are grown on into young plants for sale.

clue.text: Twenty runs is notable for me!

definitions.text: Twenty runs is notable for me!

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket fan exclaims that a quick twenty is worth a mention.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the person who records runs at cricket: anything worth noting is noted by them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket scorer writes down every run, so for them each run is literally notable, something to be noted.

clue.text: Consider carefully sales of pastry?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... an idea in the mind
second meaning: a company's sales total, with a nod to the fruit-filled pastry of the same name

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the second definition is a business's sales figure, and that same word is also a folded pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something over is to mull it; turnover is total takings, and an apple turnover is a pastry.

clue.text: Stop ticket-collector? That shows some nerve

definitions.note: optic is an adjective, as in optic nerve, the nerve of sight

indicators.note: shows means displays, so the letters are on display inside the words before

explanation.surface: Someone blocks a ticket inspector, a brazen move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows some nerve' reads as an idiom for cheek, but the nerve is the one serving the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The optic nerve carries signals from the eye to the brain, so optic names that particular nerve.

clue.text: Deliberate trick by team with little resistance

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A team plays a deliberate trick to meet little opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate as a verb means to think something over, the same as consider.

clue.text: Catch retiring business associate right away

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word runs backwards
away means removed, so the letter named just before it is taken out

parts.note: a partner is a co-owner in a firm

explanation.surface: A retiring company partner is caught out once things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' sounds like leaving the firm but asks for the word to run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch someone by trickery, as in a trap.

clue.text: Source of alternative energy in the past

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: Green power, the alternative energy source, was used in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, as in years ago, so it describes something in the past.

clue.text: Lively lady set about US university in front of Edward? It's true

definitions.note: adverb defined by a clause; admittedly means it is true that

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the outer letters surround the inner ones
lively letters jump about into a fresh order
in front of places the university abbreviation directly ahead of the name

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A vivacious woman confronts an American college before Edward, insisting it is so.
explanation.walkthrough: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The jumbled four letters split two and two to wrap round the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittedly concedes a point, meaning roughly 'it is true that', so the phrase can stand in for it.

clue.text: Heard cheers in Italy for a dog

indicators.note: heard means we go by what the ear picks up, not the spelling

parts.note: ciao is the Italian greeting or farewell, used like cheers

explanation.surface: An Italian greeting is overheard being offered to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The chow, or chow chow, is a Chinese breed of dog with a blue-black tongue.
